newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson sees mobile phone users up 57 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson sees mobile phone users up 57 pct.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group AB LM Ericsson said on Monday it expected 137 million mobile phone subscribers at the end of 1996, a 57 percent increase from the previous year.
It also said in a statement that it saw 480 million subscribers worldwide by the end of the year 2000 and 590 million by the end of 2001.
The company said years 1997, 1998 and 1999 are predicted to have about 205, 285 and 380 million subscribers respectively.
Geographically, North America was the largest market in 1996 with an estimated 47 million subscribers followed by Asia-Pacific with 42 million and Western Europe with 36 million.
"With its very high growth rate, Asia-Pacific will surpass North America in 1997 with an expected 68 million against 61," Ericsson said.
Of the estimated increase of close to 50 million in 1996, 33 million, or 65 percent, were digital subscribers.
Analogue sales were expected to peak in 1998.
Seen over a five-year period, 1996 to 2001, digital subscribers are expected to grow 10-fold, from 50 million to 500 million, Ericsson said.

Of the 33 million net increase in digital subscribers in 1996, 98 percent were in Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA) based technologies, Global System for Mobile telecommunications (GSM), Digital Advanced Mobile Phone Service (D-AMPS) and Pacific Digital Cellular (PDC).
Ericsson belongs to the companies promoting the TDMA system, as opposed to the Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) system. CDMA mainly exists in South Korea and the U.S..
